references.text: Abraham instructs the servant to travel to his land and relatives to find a wife for Isaac – the direct context for the journey in v.10
Nahor's children and family, including Bethuel (Rebekah's father), who live in the city where the servant travels
Abraham's family moves from Ur of the Chaldeans to Haran in Mesopotamia – the background for 'Aram Naharaim' and 'Nahor's city'
Abraham's great wealth – relevant because the servant had 'all his master's goods in his hand'
Joseph sends donkeys loaded with gifts, parallel to the servant's camels loaded with his master's goods
Aram Naharaim is mentioned as Balaam's homeland – a geographical parallel to the destination in Gen 24:10
